title: What Is FEFO? First-Expired, First-Out Explained for Pharmacies
excerpt: FEFO (First-Expired, First-Out) is a stock rotation rule that ships the batch closest to expiry first. This guide explains how it works, why it matters, and how to run it in a Kenyan pharmacy without spreadsheets.
author: kxbyte

cover.alt: Pharmacist checking expiry dates on medicine boxes

toc.text: Why FEFO matters in a pharmacy
How to run FEFO day to day

faq.a: FEFO stands for First-Expired, First-Out. It is a stock rotation rule where the batch with the earliest expiry date is sold or used first.

faq.q: Is FEFO the same as FIFO?
faq.a: No. FIFO rotates by arrival date — the oldest stock leaves first. FEFO rotates by expiry date — the batch closest to expiring leaves first. In a pharmacy, FEFO is safer because a newer batch can expire sooner than an older one.

faq.q: Does FEFO apply to non-medicine products?
faq.a: Yes. Any product with a shelf life benefits from FEFO — food, cosmetics, chemicals, and laboratory reagents included.
